lessons.title: Countries, Nationalities and Languages of the Arab World
lessons.summary: Name the twenty-two Arab League states, build their nationality adjectives with the nisba, and describe the region's languages accurately.
objectives: Name the twenty-two Arab League countries and their nationalities.
Form a nationality adjective with the nisba ending ـِيٌّ / ـِيَّةٌ.
Recognise that several country names are diptotes and take no tanwīn.
Describe language use across the region without treating it as uniform.
success: I add ـِيٌّ for a masculine nationality and ـِيَّةٌ for a feminine one.
I write مِصْرُ، لُبْنَانُ and قَطَرُ without tanwīn, and مِصْرَ in the genitive.
I distinguish الفُصْحَى from the spoken dialects.
I mention Amazigh and Kurdish as languages of the region, not only Arabic.

teach.title: The nisba builds the nationality
teach.text: Take the country, drop any article or ending, and add ـِيٌّ for a man or ـِيَّةٌ for a woman: مِصْر becomes مِصْرِيٌّ and مِصْرِيَّةٌ. The shadda on the yāʾ is part of the ending, not an optional decoration.

teach.title: Several country names are diptotes
teach.text: مِصْرُ، لُبْنَانُ، قَطَرُ، عُمَانُ، تُونُسُ and فِلَسْطِينُ take no tanwīn and use a fatḥa where you would expect a kasra: مِنْ مِصْرَ، فِي لُبْنَانَ. Writing مِصْرٍ is a visible error.

grammar.title: The nisba, diptotes and describing a region
grammar.arabic: النِّسْبَةُ وَالمَمْنُوعُ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ وَوَصْفُ المِنْطَقَةِ
grammar.overview: Three systems carry this lesson: forming the nationality, handling country names that refuse tanwīn, and choosing past or present according to whether you describe history or the present day.

rules.heading: Forming the nisba
rules.explanation: The ending carries a shadda on the yāʾ. A final tāʾ marbūṭa or article is dropped first.

rules.heading: Diptote country names
rules.formula: no tanwīn; fatḥa instead of kasra
rules.explanation: A diptote takes a ḍamma when nominative and a fatḥa in both the accusative and the genitive.

rules.heading: Past for history, present for today
rules.explanation: Use the past for what happened, and the present for what is currently true. Mixing them deliberately is what a strong cultural text does.
examples: نَشَأَتِ الحَضَارَةُ العَرَبِيَّةُ فِي هٰذِهِ المِنْطَقَةِ
تُعَدُّ العَرَبِيَّةُ مِنْ أَكْثَرِ اللُّغَاتِ انْتِشَارًا

rules.heading: Describing language use accurately
rules.explanation: Arabic is not the only language of the region. Name co-official languages and qualify claims rather than generalising.
examples: الأَمَازِيغِيَّةُ لُغَةٌ رَسْمِيَّةٌ فِي المَغْرِبِ وَالجَزَائِرِ
تُسْتَعْمَلُ الكُرْدِيَّةُ إِلَى جَانِبِ العَرَبِيَّةِ فِي العِرَاقِ

quiz.prompt: Choose the accurate masculine nationality for المَغْرِب.
quiz.feedback: The masculine nisba ends in ـِيٌّ with a shadda.

quiz.prompt: Choose the accurate feminine nationality for تُونُس.
quiz.feedback: The feminine nisba adds tāʾ marbūṭa after the ـِيّ ending.

quiz.prompt: Complete: أَنَا مِنْ ___.
quiz.feedback: لُبْنَان is a diptote, so the genitive takes a fatḥa and no tanwīn.

quiz.prompt: Complete: زُرْتُ ___ فِي الصَّيْفِ المَاضِي.
quiz.feedback: مِصْر is a diptote; the accusative is a bare fatḥa.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence describes history accurately?
options: نَشَأَتِ الحَضَارَةُ العَرَبِيَّةُ فِي هٰذِهِ المِنْطَقَةِ.
تَنْشَأُ الحَضَارَةُ العَرَبِيَّةُ فِي هٰذِهِ المِنْطَقَةِ.
سَتَنْشَأُ الحَضَارَةُ العَرَبِيَّةُ فِي هٰذِهِ المِنْطَقَةِ.
quiz.feedback: A completed historical event takes the past tense.

quiz.prompt: Which statement about language is accurate?
options: الأَمَازِيغِيَّةُ لُغَةٌ رَسْمِيَّةٌ فِي المَغْرِبِ وَالجَزَائِرِ.
العَرَبِيَّةُ هِيَ اللُّغَةُ الوَحِيدَةُ فِي كُلِّ الدُّوَلِ العَرَبِيَّةِ.
لَا تُوجَدُ لَهَجَاتٌ فِي العَالَمِ العَرَبِيِّ.
quiz.feedback: Amazigh is co-official in Morocco and Algeria; the region is multilingual.

quiz.prompt: What is the difference between الفُصْحَى and اللَّهَجَاتُ?
options: الفُصْحَى is the shared formal register; the dialects are spoken and vary by region.
They are two names for the same thing.
الفُصْحَى is spoken only at home.
quiz.feedback: الفُصْحَى is used in writing and formal speech; dialects differ from place to place.

quiz.prompt: Choose the accurate agreement.
quiz.feedback: Both the noun and its nisba adjective are feminine.

grammar.common_error: Adding tanwīn to a diptote — writing مِنْ لُبْنَانٍ or زُرْتُ مِصْرًا. These names take a bare fatḥa in the genitive and accusative.
grammar.challenge: Write one sentence naming a country, its nationality and one language used there, keeping every ending accurate.

builders.target: Build accurate statements about a country, its people and its languages.
builders.feedback: Each clause is accurate on its own, so any three different combinations build a valid description.

patterns.label: What to notice
patterns.tip: The nisba ending carries a shadda on the yāʾ.

patterns.label: What to notice
patterns.tip: A diptote takes a fatḥa in the genitive, with no tanwīn.

patterns.ar: تُعَدُّ العَرَبِيَّةُ مِنْ أَكْثَرِ اللُّغَاتِ انْتِشَارًا
patterns.label: What to notice
patterns.tip: A present passive for a fact that is true now.

mistakes.why: لُبْنَان is a diptote and cannot take tanwīn.
The nisba adjective must agree with its feminine noun.

mistakes.wrong: العَرَبِيَّةُ هِيَ اللُّغَةُ الوَحِيدَةُ فِي المِنْطَقَةِ.
mistakes.right: إِلَى جَانِبِ العَرَبِيَّةِ تُوجَدُ لُغَاتٌ أُخْرَى مِثْلُ الأَمَازِيغِيَّةِ وَالكُرْدِيَّةِ.
mistakes.why: The region is multilingual, so the version on the left states something untrue.

listening.title: Listening: introductions from across the region
listening.script: أَنَا سَلْمَى، وَأَنَا مَغْرِبِيَّةٌ مِنْ مَدِينَةِ الرِّبَاطِ. فِي بَيْتِنَا نَتَحَدَّثُ العَرَبِيَّةَ وَالأَمَازِيغِيَّةَ، لِأَنَّ الأَمَازِيغِيَّةَ لُغَةٌ رَسْمِيَّةٌ فِي المَغْرِبِ. وَصَدِيقِي كَرِيمٌ عِرَاقِيٌّ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ، وَيَقُولُ إِنَّ الكُرْدِيَّةَ تُسْتَعْمَلُ إِلَى جَانِبِ العَرَبِيَّةِ فِي بِلَادِهِ. أَمَّا زَمِيلَتُنَا نُورُ فَهِيَ لُبْنَانِيَّةٌ، وَقَدْ جَاءَتْ مِنْ لُبْنَانَ قَبْلَ سَنَتَيْنِ. نَحْنُ نَكْتُبُ جَمِيعًا بِالفُصْحَى، وَلٰكِنَّنَا نَتَحَدَّثُ بِلَهَجَاتٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ، وَأَحْيَانًا لَا نَفْهَمُ بَعْضَنَا بِسُرْعَةٍ.

questions.feedback: أَنَا مَغْرِبِيَّةٌ مِنْ مَدِينَةِ الرِّبَاطِ.

questions.prompt: Which languages are spoken in her home?
questions.feedback: نَتَحَدَّثُ العَرَبِيَّةَ وَالأَمَازِيغِيَّةَ.

questions.prompt: What does Karīm say about Iraq?
questions.feedback: الكُرْدِيَّةَ تُسْتَعْمَلُ إِلَى جَانِبِ العَرَبِيَّةِ فِي بِلَادِهِ.

questions.prompt: When did Nūr arrive from Lebanon?
questions.feedback: جَاءَتْ مِنْ لُبْنَانَ قَبْلَ سَنَتَيْنِ.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about writing and speaking?
options: They all write in fuṣḥā but speak different dialects
They all speak the same dialect
questions.feedback: نَكْتُبُ جَمِيعًا بِالفُصْحَى، وَلٰكِنَّنَا نَتَحَدَّثُ بِلَهَجَاتٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ.

reading.title: Reading: one region, many languages
reading.text: تَضُمُّ جَامِعَةُ الدُّوَلِ العَرَبِيَّةِ اثْنَتَيْنِ وَعِشْرِينَ دَوْلَةً، تَمْتَدُّ مِنَ المُحِيطِ الأَطْلَسِيِّ غَرْبًا إِلَى الخَلِيجِ شَرْقًا. وَتُعَدُّ العَرَبِيَّةُ الفُصْحَى اللُّغَةَ المُشْتَرَكَةَ فِي الكِتَابَةِ وَالإِعْلَامِ وَالتَّعْلِيمِ. أَمَّا فِي الحَيَاةِ اليَوْمِيَّةِ فَيَتَحَدَّثُ النَّاسُ لَهَجَاتٍ مُخْتَلِفَةً تَخْتَلِفُ مِنْ بَلَدٍ إِلَى بَلَدٍ، وَأَحْيَانًا مِنْ مَدِينَةٍ إِلَى مَدِينَةٍ. وَإِلَى جَانِبِ العَرَبِيَّةِ تُوجَدُ لُغَاتٌ أُخْرَى: فَالأَمَازِيغِيَّةُ لُغَةٌ رَسْمِيَّةٌ فِي المَغْرِبِ وَالجَزَائِرِ، وَالكُرْدِيَّةُ لُغَةٌ رَسْمِيَّةٌ فِي العِرَاقِ. وَلَيْسَ صَحِيحًا أَنَّ المِنْطَقَةَ ذَاتُ ثَقَافَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ؛ فَالتَّنَوُّعُ فِيهَا كَبِيرٌ.

questions.prompt: How many states are in the Arab League?
questions.feedback: تَضُمُّ … اثْنَتَيْنِ وَعِشْرِينَ دَوْلَةً.

questions.prompt: Where is fuṣḥā used?
questions.feedback: اللُّغَةَ المُشْتَرَكَةَ فِي الكِتَابَةِ وَالإِعْلَامِ وَالتَّعْلِيمِ.

questions.prompt: What does the text say about dialects?
options: They differ between countries and sometimes between cities
questions.feedback: تَخْتَلِفُ مِنْ بَلَدٍ إِلَى بَلَدٍ، وَأَحْيَانًا مِنْ مَدِينَةٍ إِلَى مَدِينَةٍ.

questions.prompt: Where is Amazigh an official language?
questions.feedback: الأَمَازِيغِيَّةُ لُغَةٌ رَسْمِيَّةٌ فِي المَغْرِبِ وَالجَزَائِرِ.

questions.prompt: What is the text's closing point?
options: The region is not a single culture; its diversity is great
questions.feedback: وَلَيْسَ صَحِيحًا أَنَّ المِنْطَقَةَ ذَاتُ ثَقَافَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ؛ فَالتَّنَوُّعُ فِيهَا كَبِيرٌ.

prompts: اِخْتَرْ دَوْلَةً عَرَبِيَّةً. مَا عَاصِمَتُهَا؟ وَمَا جِنْسِيَّةُ أَهْلِهَا؟

مَا الفَرْقُ بَيْنَ الفُصْحَى وَاللَّهَجَاتِ؟
model: أَخْتَارُ المَغْرِبَ. عَاصِمَتُهُ الرِّبَاطُ، وَأَهْلُهُ مَغَارِبَةٌ، وَالوَاحِدُ مِنْهُمْ مَغْرِبِيٌّ.
تُسْتَعْمَلُ العَرَبِيَّةُ وَالأَمَازِيغِيَّةُ، وَالأَمَازِيغِيَّةُ لُغَةٌ رَسْمِيَّةٌ أَيْضًا، وَلَيْسَ الأَمْرُ نَفْسَهُ فِي كُلِّ الدُّوَلِ.

writing.prompt: Write about eighty words introducing one Arab country: its name, its capital, the nationality of its people, the languages used there, and one accurate statement about the region's diversity.
checklist: One correctly formed nisba, matching the gender of its noun.
One diptote country name used after a preposition, with no tanwīn.
One sentence naming a language other than Arabic.
One qualified statement about diversity rather than a generalisation.
writing.model: مِنْ أَجْمَلِ الدُّوَلِ العَرَبِيَّةِ المَغْرِبُ، وَعَاصِمَتُهُ الرِّبَاطُ. وَأَهْلُهُ مَغَارِبَةٌ، وَالطَّالِبُ مِنْهُمْ مَغْرِبِيٌّ وَالطَّالِبَةُ مَغْرِبِيَّةٌ. تُسْتَعْمَلُ فِيهِ العَرَبِيَّةُ وَالأَمَازِيغِيَّةُ، وَالأَمَازِيغِيَّةُ لُغَةٌ رَسْمِيَّةٌ هُنَاكَ. وَقَدْ زُرْتُ مِصْرَ أَيْضًا قَبْلَ سَنَتَيْنِ، وَلَاحَظْتُ أَنَّ اللَّهْجَةَ تَخْتَلِفُ كَثِيرًا عَنْ لَهْجَةِ المَغْرِبِ. نَكْتُبُ جَمِيعًا بِالفُصْحَى، وَلٰكِنَّنَا نَتَحَدَّثُ بِلَهَجَاتٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ. وَلَيْسَ صَحِيحًا أَنَّ المِنْطَقَةَ ذَاتُ ثَقَافَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ؛ فَالتَّنَوُّعُ فِيهَا كَبِيرٌ جِدًّا.

teach.title: Each cultural verb keeps its own preposition
teach.text: يَعْتَادُ عَلَى، يَتَمَسَّكُ بِـ، يَنْتَمِي إِلَى، يَتَكَيَّفُ مَعَ. Learn the verb and the preposition as one unit; swapping them is the most common error in this topic.

teach.title: Describe what you observed, not what everyone does
teach.text: Customs vary between countries, between regions and between families. Write فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ or أَحْيَانًا rather than كُلُّ العَرَبِ. A sentence beginning “All Arabs…” is a generalisation, and it is almost always inaccurate.

grammar.title: Cultural verbs, contrast and qualification
grammar.overview: Three things to control: the preposition on each cultural verb, the structure of a contrast, and the hedge that keeps your claim honest.

rules.heading: Cultural verbs and their prepositions
rules.formula: يَعْتَادُ عَلَى · يَتَمَسَّكُ بِـ · يَنْتَمِي إِلَى · يَتَكَيَّفُ مَعَ
rules.explanation: Each preposition is fixed, and the noun after it is genitive.

rules.heading: Contrast with بَيْنَمَا
rules.explanation: بَيْنَمَا joins two full clauses that genuinely differ. It is not used for a simple list.
examples: يُقَدَّمُ القَهْوَةُ أَوَّلًا فِي بَعْضِ البُلْدَانِ، بَيْنَمَا يُقَدَّمُ الشَّايُ فِي غَيْرِهَا

rules.heading: Two-sided comparison
rules.explanation: This pair balances two aspects of the same topic and is valued in the Range criterion.
examples: مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ تَتَغَيَّرُ العَادَاتُ، وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى تَبْقَى القِيَمُ

rules.heading: Hedging a cultural claim
rules.explanation: A hedge turns a false universal into an accurate observation.
examples: فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ يُقَبِّلُ الأَبْنَاءُ رَأْسَ الجَدِّ

grammar.common_error: Beginning a sentence with كُلُّ العَرَبِ. Customs differ by country, by region and by family, so a universal claim is almost always wrong. Use فِي بَعْضِ … or أَحْيَانًا instead.

objectives: Name the customs of Ramadan and the two Eids with precise vocabulary.

teach.title: The passive changes the vowels, not the letters
teach.text: يُزَيِّنُ becomes يُزَيَّنُ, and يُوَزِّعُ becomes تُوَزَّعُ. Arabic marks the passive inside the word, so the doer disappears entirely. This is why cultural descriptions use it so often: the custom matters more than who performs it.

teach.title: General custom in the present, personal memory in the past
teach.text: يَصُومُ المُسْلِمُونَ فِي رَمَضَانَ describes what generally happens. صُمْتُ لِأَوَّلِ مَرَّةٍ عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ فِي السَّابِعَةِ describes your own experience. Keep the two apart and your writing becomes much clearer.

grammar.title: The cultural passive and tense choice
grammar.overview: One new structure and one choice: form the passive by changing the vowel pattern, and decide between present for the general custom and past for your own memory.

rules.heading: Forming the present passive
rules.explanation: The prefix takes a ḍamma and the letter before the ending takes a fatḥa. No extra word is added.

rules.heading: The passive verb agrees with the thing affected
rules.explanation: What was the object becomes the subject and is nominative. The verb agrees with it in gender.

rules.heading: Present for the general custom
rules.explanation: Use the present for what happens each year, and add a hedge where the custom is regional.

rules.heading: Past for personal experience
rules.explanation: صَامَ is hollow, so the middle vowel shortens: صُمْتُ، صُمْنَا.

teach.title: The Arab world is not religiously uniform
teach.text: Alongside Muslim majorities there are long-established Christian communities in Egypt, Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, Iraq and Palestine, and Jewish communities in several countries, notably Morocco and Tunisia. teach.text: مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ opens one side, وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى opens the other, and عِلَاوَةً عَلَى ذٰلِكَ adds a further point. Examiners reward this structure because it shows you can hold two ideas at once.

listening.script: فِي الصَّيْفِ المَاضِي حَضَرْتُ مِهْرَجَانًا ثَقَافِيًّا فِي مَسْرَحٍ أَثَرِيٍّ. شَاهَدْنَا عُرُوضًا رَائِعَةً مِنْ رَقْصٍ شَعْبِيٍّ وَمُوسِيقَى تَقْلِيدِيَّةٍ، وَلَبِسَ المُمَثِّلُونَ أَزْيَاءً تَقْلِيدِيَّةً جَمِيلَةً. وَفِي المَدِينَةِ نَفْسِهَا تُوجَدُ كَنِيسَةٌ قَدِيمَةٌ وَمَسْجِدٌ كَبِيرٌ فِي الشَّارِعِ نَفْسِهِ. وَفِي عِيدِ المِيلَادِ يَحْتَفِلُ الجِيرَانُ المَسِيحِيُّونَ، وَيُقَامُ القُدَّاسُ فِي الكَنِيسَةِ، وَيُشَارِكُهُمْ بَعْضُ الأَصْدِقَاءِ فِي التَّهْنِئَةِ. يُشَارُ إِلَى أَنَّ التَّنَوُّعَ الدِّينِيَّ قَدِيمٌ فِي المِنْطَقَةِ، وَلٰكِنَّ الأَمْرَ يَخْتَلِفُ مِنْ بَلَدٍ إِلَى بَلَدٍ.

reading.title: Reading: a region of many celebrations
reading.text: لَا يَقْتَصِرُ الاحْتِفَالُ فِي العَالَمِ العَرَبِيِّ عَلَى الأَعْيَادِ الإِسْلَامِيَّةِ. فَفِي مِصْرَ وَلُبْنَانَ وَسُورِيَا وَالأُرْدُنِّ وَفِلَسْطِينَ وَالعِرَاقِ طَوَائِفُ مَسِيحِيَّةٌ قَدِيمَةٌ تَحْتَفِلُ بِعِيدِ المِيلَادِ وَعِيدِ القِيَامَةِ، وَيُقَامُ القُدَّاسُ فِي الكَنَائِسِ. وَفِي المَغْرِبِ وَتُونُسَ مَعَابِدُ يَهُودِيَّةٌ قَدِيمَةٌ مَا زَالَتْ قَائِمَةً. عِلَاوَةً عَلَى ذٰلِكَ تُنَوِّعُ المَهْرَجَانَاتُ الثَّقَافِيَّةُ الحَيَاةَ الفَنِّيَّةَ، فَتُقَامُ عُرُوضُ الرَّقْصِ الشَّعْبِيِّ وَالمُوسِيقَى التَّقْلِيدِيَّةِ فِي مَسَارِحَ أَثَرِيَّةٍ. مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ تَخْتَلِفُ الأَعْيَادُ بِاخْتِلَافِ الطَّوَائِفِ، وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى تَجْمَعُ النَّاسَ حَوْلَ المَائِدَةِ نَفْسِهَا. وَيُشَارُ إِلَى أَنَّ العَيْشَ المُشْتَرَكَ قَدِيمٌ، وَإِنْ كَانَ يَخْتَلِفُ مِنْ بَلَدٍ إِلَى بَلَدٍ.

lessons.summary: Describe diaspora experience with يَنْتَمِي إِلَى، يَتَكَيَّفُ مَعَ، يَحْتَفِظُ بِـ and يُوَازِنُ بَيْنَ, and compare two countries using the full comparison set.
objectives: Describe belonging and adaptation with four verbs and their fixed prepositions.
Name identity vocabulary precisely: حَنِينٌ، غُرْبَةٌ، انْتِمَاءٌ، هُوِيَّةٌ مُزْدَوَجَةٌ.
Compare two countries using أَكْثَرُ مِنْ، أَفْعَل، بَيْنَمَا and مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ.
Write about migration experience without reducing it to a single story.
success: I follow يَنْتَمِي with إِلَى، يَتَكَيَّفُ with مَعَ، يَحْتَفِظُ with بِـ and يُوَازِنُ with بَيْنَ.
I use the synthetic أَفْعَل form without adding أَكْثَرُ as well.
I distinguish مُهَاجِرٌ، لَاجِئٌ and مُوَاطِنٌ accurately.
I describe dual identity as something held together, not as a problem to solve.

Someone who left because of danger; not the same as مُهَاجِرٌ.
Feminine; the feeling of living away.

teach.title: Four verbs, four prepositions
teach.text: يَنْتَمِي إِلَى، يَتَكَيَّفُ مَعَ، يَحْتَفِظُ بِـ، يُوَازِنُ بَيْنَ. Together they describe the whole arc of diaspora experience: where you belong, how you adjust, what you keep and how you hold both sides at once.

teach.title: Do not double the comparative
teach.text: Arabic has two ways to compare. Either the synthetic أَفْعَل form — أَكْبَرُ مِنْ — or the analytical أَكْثَرُ … مِنْ with a noun. Writing أَكْثَرُ أَكْبَرُ combines both and is wrong.

grammar.title: Belonging, adaptation and comparison
grammar.overview: Four verbs each with a fixed preposition, and two comparison systems that must not be mixed. Choose one comparative form and keep the noun after مِنْ genitive.

rules.heading: The four diaspora verbs
rules.formula: يَنْتَمِي إِلَى · يَتَكَيَّفُ مَعَ · يَحْتَفِظُ بِـ · يُوَازِنُ بَيْنَ
rules.explanation: Each preposition is fixed and takes the genitive. يُوَازِنُ بَيْنَ is followed by two things joined with وَ.

rules.heading: The synthetic comparative
rules.explanation: The أَفْعَل form is invariable and never takes the article in this structure.

rules.heading: The analytical comparative
rules.explanation: Use this when there is no أَفْعَل form available. The noun between is accusative.
examples: هٰذَا الحَيُّ أَكْثَرُ تَنَوُّعًا مِنْ غَيْرِهِ

rules.heading: Contrast and balance
rules.formula: بَيْنَمَا · مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ … وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى
rules.explanation: بَيْنَمَا joins two contrasting clauses; the balanced pair holds two sides of one idea together.
examples: أَتَحَدَّثُ العَرَبِيَّةَ فِي البَيْتِ، بَيْنَمَا أَدْرُسُ بِالإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةِ
مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أَشْعُرُ بِالحَنِينِ، وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى أُحِبُّ حَيَاتِي هُنَا

quiz.prompt: Choose the accurate comparative.
quiz.feedback: Use one comparative form; أَفْعَل takes no article in this structure.

quiz.prompt: Choose the accurate analytical comparative.
options: هٰذَا الحَيُّ أَكْثَرُ تَنَوُّعًا مِنْ غَيْرِهِ.
هٰذَا الحَيُّ أَكْثَرُ تَنَوُّعٌ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ.
هٰذَا الحَيُّ أَكْثَرُ مُتَنَوِّعٌ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ.
quiz.feedback: The noun between أَكْثَرُ and مِنْ is accusative.

quiz.prompt: What is the difference between مُهَاجِرٌ and لَاجِئٌ?
options: A migrant moved to live elsewhere; a refugee left because of danger.
They mean exactly the same thing.
A refugee is someone on holiday.
quiz.feedback: The two words describe different situations and should not be swapped.

quiz.prompt: Choose the balanced description of dual identity.
options: مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أَشْعُرُ بِالحَنِينِ، وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى أُحِبُّ حَيَاتِي هُنَا.
لَا يُمْكِنُ أَنْ يَنْتَمِيَ الإِنْسَانُ إِلَى ثَقَافَتَيْنِ.
quiz.feedback: The balanced pair holds both feelings together rather than treating one as a problem.

grammar.common_error: Combining both comparative systems — أَكْثَرُ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ. Choose either the أَفْعَل form or أَكْثَرُ with an accusative noun, never both.
grammar.challenge: Write one sentence with a synthetic comparative and one with an analytical comparative, then join two of your ideas with بَيْنَمَا.

builders.target: Build accurate statements about belonging, adaptation and comparison.

listening.title: Listening: growing up between two places
listening.script: أَنَا مِنَ الجِيلِ الثَّانِي فِي الجَالِيَةِ العَرَبِيَّةِ هُنَا. وُلِدْتُ فِي هٰذِهِ المَدِينَةِ، وَلٰكِنَّ أُسْرَتِي جَاءَتْ مِنَ المَغْرِبِ قَبْلَ ثَلَاثِينَ سَنَةً. أَنْتَمِي إِلَى ثَقَافَتَيْنِ، وَأُوَازِنُ بَيْنَهُمَا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. فِي البَيْتِ نَتَحَدَّثُ العَرَبِيَّةَ، بَيْنَمَا أَدْرُسُ وَأَعْمَلُ بِالإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةِ. تَحْتَفِظُ أُمِّي بِعَادَاتِهَا وَبِمَطْبَخِهَا، وَقَدْ تَكَيَّفَتْ مَعَ الحَيَاةِ هُنَا بِسُرْعَةٍ. أَحْيَانًا أَشْعُرُ بِالحَنِينِ إِلَى بَلَدِ أُسْرَتِي، وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى أُحِبُّ حَيَاتِي هُنَا كَثِيرًا. لَيْسَتِ الهُوِيَّةُ المُزْدَوَجَةُ مُشْكِلَةً؛ هِيَ ثَرْوَةٌ فِي رَأْيِي.

reading.title: Reading: communities, not one story
reading.text: تَعِيشُ جَالِيَاتٌ عَرَبِيَّةٌ فِي بُلْدَانٍ كَثِيرَةٍ حَوْلَ العَالَمِ. وَقَدْ وَصَلَ بَعْضُ النَّاسِ مُهَاجِرِينَ بَحْثًا عَنْ عَمَلٍ أَوْ دِرَاسَةٍ، بَيْنَمَا وَصَلَ آخَرُونَ لَاجِئِينَ هَرَبًا مِنَ الحَرْبِ؛ وَالكَلِمَتَانِ لَيْسَتَا مُتَرَادِفَتَيْنِ. يَحْتَفِظُ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ الأُسَرِ بِلُغَتِهِمْ وَإِرْثِهِمُ الثَّقَافِيِّ، وَفِي الوَقْتِ نَفْسِهِ يَتَكَيَّفُونَ مَعَ مُجْتَمَعَاتٍ جَدِيدَةٍ. أَمَّا الجِيلُ الثَّانِي فَيَنْتَمِي إِلَى ثَقَافَتَيْنِ، وَيُوَازِنُ بَيْنَهُمَا فِي حَيَاتِهِ اليَوْمِيَّةِ. مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ يَشْعُرُ بَعْضُهُمْ بِالحَنِينِ وَالغُرْبَةِ، وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى يَرَوْنَ فِي الهُوِيَّةِ المُزْدَوَجَةِ ثَرْوَةً. وَتَجَارِبُ النَّاسِ مُخْتَلِفَةٌ، فَلَا تُوجَدُ قِصَّةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ تَصِفُ الجَمِيعَ.

questions.prompt: Why did some people arrive?
questions.feedback: وَصَلَ بَعْضُ النَّاسِ مُهَاجِرِينَ بَحْثًا عَنْ عَمَلٍ أَوْ دِرَاسَةٍ.

questions.prompt: What does the text say about the two words?
questions.feedback: وَالكَلِمَتَانِ لَيْسَتَا مُتَرَادِفَتَيْنِ.

questions.prompt: What do many families keep?
questions.feedback: يَحْتَفِظُ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ الأُسَرِ بِلُغَتِهِمْ وَإِرْثِهِمُ الثَّقَافِيِّ.

questions.prompt: What is the closing point?
options: Experiences differ; no single story describes everyone
questions.feedback: فَلَا تُوجَدُ قِصَّةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ تَصِفُ الجَمِيعَ.

writing.prompt: Write eighty to ninety words comparing life in two countries, drawing on the diaspora vocabulary. Use at least three of the four verbs with their prepositions, both comparative systems, and a balanced statement about dual identity.

lessons.title: Arabic Around the World — The Language's Global Reach
lessons.arabic: العَرَبِيَّةُ حَوْلَ العَالَمِ — الانْتِشَارُ العَالَمِيُّ لِلُّغَةِ
lessons.summary: Use formal statistical language to describe Arabic's global status, trace words that travelled into other languages, and argue for the value of learning it.
objectives: Describe Arabic's global status using يُعَدُّ، يَبْلُغُ and يُمَثِّلُ.
Handle numbers accurately with مِلْيُون and the counted noun.
Name words that travelled from Arabic into other languages.
Argue the value of learning Arabic using يُثْرِي and يُوَسِّعُ.
success: I follow يُعَدُّ … مِنْ with a genitive plural.
I write أَرْبَعُمِئَةِ مِلْيُونِ مُتَحَدِّثٍ with each noun in the right case.
I can name several words of Arabic origin and say what they became.
I give يُثْرِي and يُوَسِّعُ a direct object without a preposition.

teach.title: Formal statistics have their own verbs
teach.text: يُعَدُّ … مِنْ places something in a category, يَبْلُغُ gives a figure, and يُمَثِّلُ states a proportion. These three carry almost every statistical sentence you will need in a formal text.

teach.title: Words travel, and the route is often long
teach.text: الجَبْر، الكِيمْيَاء، قَهْوَة، سُكَّر، صِفْر and قُطْن all reached other languages from or through Arabic, sometimes via Latin, Italian or Spanish. Say that a word reached another language; avoid claiming an exact path unless you have checked it.

grammar.title: Statistical language and the direct object
grammar.overview: Three formal verbs, one number pattern and two Form II/IV verbs that take direct objects. Watch the case on every counted noun.

rules.heading: يُعَدُّ مِنْ
rules.explanation: A passive verb placing something within a group. The following noun is genitive.
examples: تُعَدُّ العَرَبِيَّةُ مِنْ أَكْثَرِ اللُّغَاتِ انْتِشَارًا
يُعَدُّ الخَطُّ العَرَبِيُّ مِنْ أَجْمَلِ الفُنُونِ

rules.heading: Numbers with مِلْيُون
rules.explanation: مِلْيُون behaves as the counted noun and is followed by a singular genitive.

rules.heading: يُمَثِّلُ with a direct object
rules.explanation: Form II takes a direct object with no preposition.

rules.heading: يُثْرِي and يُوَسِّعُ
rules.explanation: Both take direct objects. Do not add a preposition after them.

listening.title: Listening: why one student chose Arabic
listening.script: تُعَدُّ العَرَبِيَّةُ مِنْ أَكْثَرِ اللُّغَاتِ انْتِشَارًا فِي العَالَمِ، وَهِيَ إِحْدَى لُغَاتِ الأُمَمِ المُتَّحِدَةِ الرَّسْمِيَّةِ. وَيَبْلُغُ عَدَدُ المُتَحَدِّثِينَ بِهَا مَلَايِينَ كَثِيرَةً فِي قَارَّاتٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ. اخْتَرْتُ دِرَاسَتَهَا لِأَنَّهَا تَفْتَحُ أَبْوَابًا فِي التَّرْجَمَةِ وَالدِّبْلُومَاسِيَّةِ وَالتِّجَارَةِ. وَقَدْ فَاجَأَنِي أَنَّ كَلِمَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً وَصَلَتْ مِنَ العَرَبِيَّةِ إِلَى لُغَاتٍ أُخْرَى، مِثْلَ الجَبْرِ وَالكِيمْيَاءِ وَالقَهْوَةِ وَالسُّكَّرِ وَالصِّفْرِ. تُثْرِي اللُّغَةُ تَفْكِيرِي، وَتُوَسِّعُ آفَاقِي، وَتُمَثِّلُ جِسْرًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ ثَقَافَاتٍ جَدِيدَةٍ.

reading.title: Reading: a language that travelled
reading.text: تُعَدُّ العَرَبِيَّةُ مِنْ أَقْدَمِ اللُّغَاتِ الحَيَّةِ وَأَوْسَعِهَا انْتِشَارًا، وَتُسْتَعْمَلُ لُغَةً رَسْمِيَّةً فِي دُوَلٍ كَثِيرَةٍ. وَقَدِ انْتَقَلَتْ كَلِمَاتٌ عَرَبِيَّةٌ إِلَى لُغَاتٍ أُخْرَى عَبْرَ التِّجَارَةِ وَالتَّرْجَمَةِ وَالعُلُومِ، فَوَصَلَتْ كَلِمَاتٌ مِثْلُ الجَبْرِ وَالكِيمْيَاءِ إِلَى الأُورُوبِّيَّةِ عَنْ طَرِيقِ التَّرْجَمَاتِ العِلْمِيَّةِ، وَوَصَلَتِ القَهْوَةُ وَالسُّكَّرُ وَالقُطْنُ مَعَ التِّجَارَةِ. وَيُشَارُ إِلَى أَنَّ الصِّفْرَ انْتَقَلَ مَعَ نِظَامِ الأَرْقَامِ الَّذِي غَيَّرَ الحِسَابَ. عِلَاوَةً عَلَى ذٰلِكَ تُمَثِّلُ العَرَبِيَّةُ اليَوْمَ قِيمَةً مِهْنِيَّةً فِي التَّرْجَمَةِ وَالدِّبْلُومَاسِيَّةِ. وَلَيْسَ الطَّرِيقُ الَّذِي سَلَكَتْهُ كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ وَاضِحًا تَمَامًا، وَلٰكِنَّ التَّأْثِيرَ اللُّغَوِيَّ ثَابِتٌ.

lessons.summary: Bring the whole D1–D6 grammar system into one integrated text: three tenses, relative clauses, comparatives, passives and formal connectors.
objectives: Produce accurate past, present and future in a single connected text.
Use a relative clause with الَّذِي or الَّتِي agreeing with its noun.
Combine a passive, a comparative and a formal connector without losing accuracy.
Identify your own remaining grammar targets before the final assessment.

teach.title: The relative pronoun looks backwards
teach.text: الَّذِي and الَّتِي agree with the noun before them, not with whatever follows. المَدِينَةُ الَّتِي زُرْتُهَا — feminine noun, feminine pronoun. A definite noun needs the relative pronoun; an indefinite one does not.

teach.title: One structure at a time, then combine
teach.text: Most errors at this level come from stacking: two comparatives, or a passive that keeps its object accusative. Write the clause with one structure, check it, then join it to the next with a connector.

grammar.title: The whole system in one text
grammar.overview: Four checks carry this lesson: does each verb match its time phrase, does each relative pronoun agree, is only one comparative used, and does each passive have a nominative subject.

rules.heading: Three tenses, three markers
rules.formula: past time phrase → past · الآنَ → present · سَـ / سَوْفَ → future
rules.explanation: Each clause carries its own time reference, so the tense can change from clause to clause within one sentence.
examples: فِي المَاضِي احْتَفَلْنَا فِي البَيْتِ، وَالآنَ نَحْتَفِلُ مَعَ الجِيرَانِ

rules.heading: Relative clauses
rules.explanation: The pronoun agrees with the preceding noun in gender and number. After an indefinite noun no pronoun is used.

rules.heading: Negating the future
rules.explanation: لَنْ replaces سَـ and puts the verb in the subjunctive, so the final ḍamma becomes a fatḥa.

rules.heading: Formal connectors
rules.formula: عَلَى الرَّغْمِ مِنْ + genitive · شَرِيطَةَ أَنْ + subjunctive
rules.explanation: Each connector governs what follows it. عِلَاوَةً عَلَى ذٰلِكَ simply adds a point.
examples: عَلَى الرَّغْمِ مِنْ بُعْدِ المَسَافَةِ، نَحْتَفِظُ بِعَادَاتِنَا

quiz.prompt: Choose the accurate relative clause.
quiz.feedback: The pronoun agrees with the feminine noun before it, which must be definite.

quiz.prompt: Choose the accurate future negation.
quiz.feedback: لَنْ takes the subjunctive and the object stays accusative.

quiz.prompt: Choose the sentence where every verb matches its time phrase.
options: فِي المَاضِي احْتَفَلْنَا فِي البَيْتِ، وَالآنَ نَحْتَفِلُ مَعَ الجِيرَانِ، وَسَنَحْتَفِلُ غَدًا فِي المَرْكَزِ.
فِي المَاضِي نَحْتَفِلُ فِي البَيْتِ، وَالآنَ احْتَفَلْنَا، وَسَنَحْتَفِلُ أَمْسِ.
quiz.feedback: Each clause carries the tense its own time phrase requires.

quiz.feedback: The affected noun becomes the nominative subject.

quiz.feedback: عَلَى الرَّغْمِ مِنْ is followed by a genitive noun.

المِهْرَجَانُ الَّتِي حَضَرْنَاهُ كَانَ أَكْثَرُ أَكْبَرَ، وَسَعُدْنَا إِلَيْهِ.
مِهْرَجَانٌ الَّذِي حَضَرْنَاهُ أَكْبَرُ وَسَنَعُودُ أَمْسِ.
quiz.feedback: The relative pronoun agrees, one comparative is used, and the future is marked correctly.

listening.title: Listening: one family across three tenses
listening.script: فِي المَاضِي كَانَتْ أُسْرَتِي تَحْتَفِلُ بِالعِيدِ فِي القَرْيَةِ الَّتِي وُلِدَ فِيهَا جَدِّي. وَكَانَتِ الشَّوَارِعُ تُزَيَّنُ، وَتُتَبَادَلُ التَّهَانِي بَيْنَ الجِيرَانِ. أَمَّا الآنَ فَنَحْتَفِلُ هُنَا مَعَ الجَالِيَةِ، وَنَحْتَفِظُ بِالعَادَاتِ نَفْسِهَا عَلَى الرَّغْمِ مِنْ بُعْدِ المَسَافَةِ. وَالاحْتِفَالُ الَّذِي نُنَظِّمُهُ اليَوْمَ أَصْغَرُ مِنَ السَّابِقِ، وَلٰكِنَّهُ أَكْثَرُ تَنَوُّعًا. وَفِي العَامِ القَادِمِ سَنَدْعُو أَصْدِقَاءَنَا لِكَيْ يَتَعَرَّفُوا عَلَى ثَقَافَتِنَا. وَلَنْ نَتَخَلَّى عَنْ لُغَتِنَا، شَرِيطَةَ أَنْ نَسْتَمِرَّ فِي تَعْلِيمِهَا لِأَبْنَائِنَا.

reading.title: Reading: a text that uses everything
reading.text: تُعَدُّ المُجْتَمَعَاتُ الَّتِي تَجْمَعُ ثَقَافَاتٍ مُخْتَلِفَةً مِنْ أَغْنَى المُجْتَمَعَاتِ. فِي المَاضِي كَانَ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ الأُسَرِ يَحْتَفِظُ بِعَادَاتِهِ دُونَ أَنْ يُشَارِكَهُ الجِيرَانُ، أَمَّا اليَوْمَ فَتُقَامُ مَهْرَجَانَاتٌ مُشْتَرَكَةٌ تُزَيَّنُ فِيهَا السَّاحَاتُ وَتُتَبَادَلُ فِيهَا الأَطْعِمَةُ. وَالمِهْرَجَانُ الَّذِي حَضَرْتُهُ العَامَ المَاضِيَ كَانَ أَصْغَرَ مِنْ مِهْرَجَانِ هٰذَا العَامِ، وَلٰكِنَّهُ كَانَ أَكْثَرَ دِفْئًا. عِلَاوَةً عَلَى ذٰلِكَ يُؤَدِّي هٰذَا التَّوَاصُلُ إِلَى فَهْمٍ أَفْضَلَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ. وَفِي المُسْتَقْبَلِ سَتَزْدَادُ هٰذِهِ المُنَاسَبَاتُ، شَرِيطَةَ أَنْ تُدْعَمَ مِنَ المَدَارِسِ وَالبَلَدِيَّاتِ. وَلَنْ يَخْسَرَ أَحَدٌ هُوِيَّتَهُ بِسَبَبِ ذٰلِكَ؛ بَلْ يَتَعَلَّمُ كُلُّ طَرَفٍ مِنَ الآخَرِ.

questions.prompt: How are mixed-culture societies described?
questions.feedback: تُعَدُّ … مِنْ أَغْنَى المُجْتَمَعَاتِ.

questions.prompt: What happens at the shared festivals?
options: The squares are decorated and food is exchanged
questions.feedback: تُزَيَّنُ فِيهَا السَّاحَاتُ وَتُتَبَادَلُ فِيهَا الأَطْعِمَةُ.

questions.prompt: How is last year's festival compared with this year's?
questions.feedback: كَانَ أَصْغَرَ مِنْ مِهْرَجَانِ هٰذَا العَامِ، وَلٰكِنَّهُ كَانَ أَكْثَرَ دِفْئًا.

questions.feedback: يُؤَدِّي هٰذَا التَّوَاصُلُ إِلَى فَهْمٍ أَفْضَلَ.

questions.feedback: شَرِيطَةَ أَنْ تُدْعَمَ مِنَ المَدَارِسِ وَالبَلَدِيَّاتِ.

lessons.summary: Read cultural texts for what the writer implies as well as what they state: tone, word choice, what is left out, and what the tense signals.

teach.title: Attitude hides in word choice
teach.text: Two writers can report the same festival. One writes مُزْدَحِمٌ (crowded), another writes نَابِضٌ بِالحَيَاةِ (full of life). The fact is the same; the attitude is not. Quote the adjective, and you have your evidence.

teach.title: What is left out is evidence too
teach.text: A travel article that describes only the old city and never the modern one has made a choice. Noticing an omission is a high-level reading skill, and it is exactly what an R3 question rewards.

grammar.title: Reading for attitude and implication
grammar.overview: Three sources of evidence: the words the writer chose, the tone across the whole text, and what the tense signals about time and completion.

rules.heading: Word choice signals attitude
rules.formula: same fact + different adjective = different attitude
rules.explanation: Positive and negative colouring is carried by adjectives and by the nouns a writer selects.

rules.heading: Tense signals time and completion
rules.explanation: A cultural text that uses the past presents something as history; the present presents it as a current reality.

rules.heading: Naming the tone
rules.explanation: Judge the tone from the accumulation of choices across the text, not from one word alone.

listening.title: Listening: two travellers, one city
listening.script: المُتَحَدِّثُ الأَوَّلُ: زُرْتُ المَدِينَةَ القَدِيمَةَ وَأَعْجَبَنِي سُوقُهَا النَّابِضُ بِالحَيَاةِ. كُلُّ زَاوِيَةٍ فِيهِ تَحْكِي قِصَّةً، وَقَدِ اسْتَقْبَلَنَا النَّاسُ بِكَرَمٍ كَبِيرٍ. المُتَحَدِّثُ الثَّانِي: أَنَا زُرْتُ السُّوقَ نَفْسَهُ، وَوَجَدْتُهُ مُزْدَحِمًا وَصَاخِبًا قَلِيلًا، وَلٰكِنَّ المَبَانِيَ التَّارِيخِيَّةَ كَانَتْ مُثِيرَةً لِلاهْتِمَامِ. لَمْ أَذْكُرِ المَطَاعِمَ لِأَنَّنِي لَمْ أُجَرِّبْهَا. يُشَارُ إِلَى أَنَّ النَّصَّيْنِ يَصِفَانِ المَكَانَ نَفْسَهُ، وَلٰكِنَّ نَبْرَةَ الأَوَّلِ احْتِفَالِيَّةٌ، بَيْنَمَا نَبْرَةُ الثَّانِي أَقْرَبُ إِلَى الحِيَادِ.

reading.title: Reading: a travel article and what it implies
reading.text: تَقَعُ هٰذِهِ المَدِينَةُ عَلَى السَّاحِلِ، وَقَدِ ازْدَهَرَتْ قَدِيمًا بِفَضْلِ التِّجَارَةِ. وَمَا زَالَتْ أَسْوَاقُهَا القَدِيمَةُ تَزْدَهِرُ اليَوْمَ، وَفِيهَا حِرَفٌ تَقْلِيدِيَّةٌ نَابِضَةٌ بِالحَيَاةِ. يَسْتَقْبِلُ أَهْلُهَا الزَّائِرِينَ بِكَرَمٍ، وَتُقَامُ فِيهَا مَهْرَجَانَاتٌ تُنَوِّعُ الحَيَاةَ الثَّقَافِيَّةَ. وَيُشِيرُ الكَاتِبُ إِلَى أَنَّ التُّرَاثَ هُنَا مَحْفُوظٌ بِعِنَايَةٍ. عَلَى الرَّغْمِ مِنْ ذٰلِكَ لَا يَذْكُرُ النَّصُّ الأَحْيَاءَ الحَدِيثَةَ وَلَا المُشْكِلَاتِ اليَوْمِيَّةَ، وَهٰذَا اخْتِيَارٌ لَهُ دَلَالَتُهُ. فَنَبْرَةُ الكَاتِبِ احْتِفَالِيَّةٌ أَكْثَرَ مِنْهَا مُحَايِدَةً، وَالقَارِئُ الجَيِّدُ يُلَاحِظُ مَا ذُكِرَ وَمَا أُغْفِلَ مَعًا.

grammar.title: Deploying the full range in one piece
grammar.arabic: تَوْظِيفُ القَوَاعِدِ كَامِلَةً فِي نَصٍّ وَاحِدٍ
grammar.overview: One text, six structures. Plan where each will appear before you write, then check them one at a time afterwards.

rules.heading: Three tenses, signalled
rules.formula: past experience → present habit → future aspiration
rules.explanation: Each section carries its own time phrase, and the verbs follow it.
examples: فِي الطُّفُولَةِ احْتَفَلْنَا فِي بَلَدِ أُسْرَتِي

rules.heading: One cultural verb, correctly governed
rules.formula: يَحْتَفِلُ بِـ · يَنْتَمِي إِلَى · يَتَمَسَّكُ بِـ · يَعْتَادُ عَلَى
rules.explanation: Choose one and get its preposition right; that is worth more than using three carelessly.

rules.heading: An opinion with a supported claim
rules.formula: لَا يُمْكِنُ إِنْكَارُ أَنَّ + accusative noun
rules.explanation: أَنَّ makes the following noun accusative. Follow the claim with a reason.
examples: لَا يُمْكِنُ إِنْكَارُ أَنَّ اللُّغَةَ جُزْءٌ مِنَ الهُوِيَّةِ

rules.heading: A passive and a formal connector
rules.formula: تُزَيَّنُ / تُتَبَادَلُ · عِلَاوَةً عَلَى ذٰلِكَ · عَلَى الرَّغْمِ مِنْ
rules.explanation: The passive subject is nominative; عَلَى الرَّغْمِ مِنْ takes a genitive noun.

teach.title: A hedge changes the answer
teach.text: If a speaker says فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ or لَيْسَ دَائِمًا, an option claiming that everyone does it is wrong. Examiners build distractors from exactly this difference.

teach.title: Track the speaker as well as the fact
teach.text: In a two-person text, note who says what as you listen. A distractor often reports something true, but attributes it to the wrong speaker.

grammar.title: Hearing tense, attribution and qualification
grammar.overview: Three things to catch at speed: which tense the verb carries, which speaker said it, and whether the claim was qualified.

rules.heading: Tense from the verb shape
rules.formula: suffix = past · prefix = present · سَـ = future
rules.explanation: The topic does not tell you the tense; the word shape does.

rules.heading: Past habit versus single event
rules.formula: كَانَ + present vs a single past verb
rules.explanation: كَانَ يَحْتَفِلُ means used to celebrate; احْتَفَلَ means celebrated once.

rules.heading: Qualified claims
rules.explanation: A qualifier narrows the claim. Any option that widens it back to everyone is wrong.

rules.heading: Attribution in a dialogue
rules.explanation: Note each claim against its speaker as you listen; decide only afterwards.

quiz.prompt: Which verb is past?
quiz.feedback: A suffix with no prefix marks the past.

quiz.feedback: كَانَ plus a present verb is a past habit.

quiz.feedback: The hedge rules out any claim about all families.

mistakes.why: كَانَ places the habit in the past.

mistakes.right: Noting each claim against its speaker while listening.
mistakes.why: Distractors often move a true fact to the wrong speaker.

listening.title: Listening: an identity across three tenses
listening.script: فِي الطُّفُولَةِ كُنَّا نَحْتَفِلُ بِالعِيدِ فِي بَلَدِ أُسْرَتِي، وَكَانَتْ جَدَّتِي تُعِدُّ الحَلْوَى بِنَفْسِهَا. وَفِي العَامِ المَاضِي زُرْنَا الأَقَارِبَ هُنَاكَ بَعْدَ غِيَابٍ طَوِيلٍ. أَمَّا الآنَ فَنَحْتَفِلُ عَادَةً فِي المَرْكَزِ الثَّقَافِيِّ مَعَ الجَالِيَةِ، وَتُزَيَّنُ القَاعَةُ وَتُتَبَادَلُ التَّهَانِي. وَفِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ تُوَزَّعُ العِيدِيَّةُ عَلَى الأَطْفَالِ، وَلٰكِنْ لَيْسَ دَائِمًا؛ فَالعَادَاتُ تَخْتَلِفُ. فِي رَأْيِي الاِنْتِمَاءُ لَا يَعْنِي مَكَانًا وَاحِدًا. وَالعَامَ القَادِمَ سَنُنَظِّمُ حَفْلًا أَكْبَرَ، وَسَنَدْعُو الجِيرَانَ لِكَيْ يَتَعَرَّفُوا عَلَى تَقَالِيدِنَا.

questions.prompt: What used to happen in childhood?
options: They celebrated Eid in the family's country
questions.feedback: كُنَّا نَحْتَفِلُ بِالعِيدِ فِي بَلَدِ أُسْرَتِي.

questions.prompt: What happened last year?
options: They visited relatives after a long absence
questions.feedback: زُرْنَا الأَقَارِبَ هُنَاكَ بَعْدَ غِيَابٍ طَوِيلٍ.

questions.prompt: Where do they usually celebrate now?
options: At the cultural centre with the community
questions.feedback: أَمَّا الآنَ فَنَحْتَفِلُ عَادَةً فِي المَرْكَزِ الثَّقَافِيِّ.

questions.prompt: How is the Eid money custom described?
options: It happens in some families, but not always
questions.feedback: فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ تُوَزَّعُ العِيدِيَّةُ … وَلٰكِنْ لَيْسَ دَائِمًا.

questions.prompt: Why will the neighbours be invited next year?
options: So they can get to know the traditions
questions.feedback: سَنَدْعُو الجِيرَانَ لِكَيْ يَتَعَرَّفُوا عَلَى تَقَالِيدِنَا.

reading.title: Reading: the transcript, annotated for tense and attribution
reading.text: اِقْرَأِ الحِوَارَ وَحَدِّدْ زَمَنَ كُلِّ فِعْلٍ وَمَنْ قَالَهُ. نُورُ: فِي الطُّفُولَةِ كُنْتُ أَتَحَدَّثُ العَرَبِيَّةَ فِي البَيْتِ فَقَطْ، وَالآنَ أَدْرُسُهَا فِي المَدْرَسَةِ أَيْضًا. سَامِي: أَمَّا أَنَا فَقَدْ تَعَلَّمْتُهَا مُتَأَخِّرًا، وَلٰكِنَّنِي تَكَيَّفْتُ بِسُرْعَةٍ. نُورُ: أَحْتَفِظُ بِلُغَتِي لِأَنَّهَا تَرْبِطُنِي بِجُذُورِي. سَامِي: وَأَنَا أَعْتَزُّ بِهَا أَيْضًا، وَفِي بَعْضِ الأَحْيَانِ أَخْلِطُ بَيْنَ اللُّغَتَيْنِ. نُورُ: هٰذَا طَبِيعِيٌّ، وَلَيْسَ دَائِمًا مُشْكِلَةً. سَامِي: فِي العَامِ القَادِمِ سَأَزُورُ بَلَدَ أُسْرَتِي، وَأَطْمَحُ إِلَى أَنْ أُتْقِنَ الفُصْحَى.

questions.prompt: Who spoke Arabic only at home in childhood?
questions.feedback: نُورُ: فِي الطُّفُولَةِ كُنْتُ أَتَحَدَّثُ العَرَبِيَّةَ فِي البَيْتِ فَقَطْ.

questions.prompt: Who learned Arabic late?
questions.feedback: سَامِي: أَمَّا أَنَا فَقَدْ تَعَلَّمْتُهَا مُتَأَخِّرًا.

questions.prompt: Who takes pride in the language?
questions.feedback: Nūr keeps it because of her roots; Sami says وَأَنَا أَعْتَزُّ بِهَا أَيْضًا.

questions.prompt: How does Nūr describe mixing the languages?
options: Natural, and not always a problem
questions.feedback: هٰذَا طَبِيعِيٌّ، وَلَيْسَ دَائِمًا مُشْكِلَةً.

questions.prompt: Which tense does Sami use for his plan?
options: Future with سَـ and أَطْمَحُ إِلَى
questions.feedback: سَأَزُورُ بَلَدَ أُسْرَتِي، وَأَطْمَحُ إِلَى أَنْ أُتْقِنَ الفُصْحَى.

prompts: مَاذَا كَانَ يَفْعَلُ المُتَحَدِّثُ فِي الطُّفُولَةِ؟
مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ الآنَ عَادَةً؟ وَهَلْ هُنَاكَ تَحَفُّظٌ فِي كَلَامِهِ؟
مَا خُطَّتُهُ لِلْعَامِ القَادِمِ؟
model: كَانَ يَحْتَفِلُ بِالعِيدِ فِي بَلَدِ أُسْرَتِهِ، وَكَانَتْ جَدَّتُهُ تُعِدُّ الحَلْوَى.
وَهَلْ قَالَ إِنَّ كُلَّ العَائِلَاتِ تَفْعَلُ ذٰلِكَ؟
لَا، قَالَ فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ وَلَيْسَ دَائِمًا، لِأَنَّ العَادَاتِ تَخْتَلِفُ.

writing.prompt: Write about seventy words summarising the listening text. Report what the speaker used to do, what they do now, how they qualified one claim, and what they will do next year.
checklist: One كَانَ plus present construction for the past habit.
Two present-tense verbs for current customs.
One reported qualification such as فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ or لَيْسَ دَائِمًا.

writing.model: فِي الطُّفُولَةِ كَانَ المُتَحَدِّثُ يَحْتَفِلُ بِالعِيدِ فِي بَلَدِ أُسْرَتِهِ، وَكَانَتْ جَدَّتُهُ تُعِدُّ الحَلْوَى بِنَفْسِهَا. وَفِي العَامِ المَاضِي زَارَ الأَقَارِبَ هُنَاكَ. أَمَّا الآنَ فَيَحْتَفِلُ عَادَةً فِي المَرْكَزِ الثَّقَافِيِّ، وَتُزَيَّنُ القَاعَةُ وَتُتَبَادَلُ التَّهَانِي. وَقَالَ إِنَّ العِيدِيَّةَ تُوَزَّعُ فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ وَلَيْسَ دَائِمًا، لِأَنَّ العَادَاتِ تَخْتَلِفُ. وَفِي العَامِ القَادِمِ سَيُنَظِّمُ حَفْلًا أَكْبَرَ، وَسَيَدْعُو الجِيرَانَ لِكَيْ يَتَعَرَّفُوا عَلَى تَقَالِيدِهِ.

mission.title: Listening Mission — Tense, Speaker and Hedge
mission.intro: Each round turns on a verb shape, a speaker or a qualifier. Decide from what was actually said.

rounds.feedback: A suffix with no prefix marks the past.
كَانَ plus a present verb.
سَـ marks the future.

rounds.prompt: You hear فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ. Which option is wrong?
rounds.feedback: The hedge rules out a universal claim.
القِيَمُ are values.
المُعْتَقَدَاتُ are beliefs.

rounds.prompt: Attribution: what should you note while listening to a dialogue?
rounds.feedback: Distractors often move a true fact to the wrong speaker.

rounds.prompt: You hear فِي رَأْيِي. What does it signal?
rounds.feedback: It marks a personal view rather than a fact.

rounds.prompt: Passive: what does تُوَزَّعُ العِيدِيَّةُ mean?
rounds.feedback: A present passive with a nominative subject.

rounds.prompt: Time phrase: which signals a present habit?

rounds.prompt: Purpose: what does لِكَيْ يَتَعَرَّفُوا express?
options: So that they get to know

الجَالِيَةُ is the community living abroad.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence reports a qualified claim accurately?
options: قَالَ إِنَّ العَادَةَ تُوجَدُ فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ.
قَالَ إِنَّ كُلَّ العَائِلَاتِ تَفْعَلُ ذٰلِكَ.
قَالَ إِنَّ أَحَدًا لَا يَفْعَلُ ذٰلِكَ.
rounds.feedback: The report keeps the speaker's own qualification.

rounds.prompt: Transfer: which summary keeps every tense and hedge right?
options: كَانَ يَحْتَفِلُ فِي الطُّفُولَةِ، وَيَحْتَفِلُ الآنَ فِي المَرْكَزِ، وَسَيُنَظِّمُ حَفْلًا أَكْبَرَ، وَالعَادَاتُ تَخْتَلِفُ.
احْتَفَلَ فِي الطُّفُولَةِ وَاحْتَفَلَ الآنَ وَاحْتَفَلَ غَدًا وَكُلُّ العَائِلَاتِ مِثْلُهُ.
سَيَحْتَفِلُ فِي الطُّفُولَةِ وَاحْتَفَلَ فِي المُسْتَقْبَلِ.
rounds.feedback: Each clause matches its time reference and the qualification is preserved.

builder_tasks.feedback: The report must keep the speaker's own qualification.

lessons.title: D6 Consolidation — Complete Review and Speaking Preparation
lessons.arabic: تَرْسِيخُ الوَحْدَةِ — مُرَاجَعَةٌ شَامِلَةٌ وَإِعْدَادُ التَّحَدُّثِ
lessons.summary: Hold a fluent topic conversation on culture and identity, deploying the full D6 range under speaking pressure, and set targets for what comes next.
objectives: Sustain a topic conversation on culture, celebration and identity.
Deploy cultural verbs, three tenses and an opinion structure while speaking.
Qualify a cultural claim in real time rather than generalising.
Name your own remaining priority before the final assessment.
success: I answer in the tense the question uses.
I get the preposition right on every cultural verb I use.
I add a reason or an example to every answer.
I hedge a cultural claim naturally instead of overstating it.

teach.title: Hedge while you speak, not afterwards
teach.text: فِي بَعْضِ البُلْدَانِ and عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي take a second to say and change an overstated claim into an accurate one. Build them into the sentence as you produce it.

teach.title: One accurate cultural verb beats three careless ones
teach.text: Examiners hear the preposition. يَحْتَفِلُ بِـ said correctly is worth more than three cultural verbs with the wrong complements.

grammar.title: The D6 system under speaking pressure
grammar.overview: A checklist you can run while speaking: mirror the tense, fix the preposition, add a reason, qualify the claim.

rules.heading: Mirror the tense of the question
rules.explanation: If the examiner asks with a past verb, answer with one. Switching to the present is the commonest avoidance pattern.
examples: صِفْ مُنَاسَبَةً مَرَرْتَ بِهَا — حَضَرْتُ حَفْلًا فِي المَرْكَزِ

rules.heading: Cultural verb plus preposition
rules.formula: يَحْتَفِلُ بِـ · يَنْتَمِي إِلَى · يَتَكَيَّفُ مَعَ
rules.explanation: Say the verb and the preposition as one unit so the pair never comes apart under pressure.

rules.heading: Extend with a reason or an example
rules.explanation: A bare answer scores little; one extension turns it into a response.

rules.heading: Qualify as you speak
rules.formula: فِي بَعْضِ … / عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي / لَيْسَ دَائِمًا
rules.explanation: A qualifier keeps a cultural statement accurate and shows control of register.
examples: فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ تُوَزَّعُ العِيدِيَّةُ، وَلَيْسَ دَائِمًا

quiz.prompt: The examiner asks: صِفْ مُنَاسَبَةً مَرَرْتَ بِهَا. Which answer is appropriate?
quiz.feedback: A past question requires a past answer.

quiz.prompt: Complete: نَحْتَفِلُ ___ العِيدِ كُلَّ سَنَةٍ.
quiz.feedback: يَحْتَفِلُ is fixed with بِـ.

quiz.prompt: Which answer is extended rather than bare?
quiz.feedback: A reason turns an answer into a response.

quiz.prompt: Which statement is appropriately qualified?
quiz.feedback: The hedge reports what some families do.

quiz.prompt: Which phrase buys thinking time in Arabic?
quiz.feedback: A short Arabic filler protects the fluency mark.

quiz.prompt: Complete: أَنْتَمِي ___ ثَقَافَتَيْنِ.
quiz.feedback: يَنْتَمِي is fixed with إِلَى.

quiz.prompt: Complete: لَا يُمْكِنُ إِنْكَارُ أَنَّ ___ ثَرْوَةٌ.
quiz.feedback: أَنَّ takes an accusative noun.

quiz.prompt: Which answer would score highest in a topic conversation?
options: حَضَرْتُ حَفْلًا فِي الطُّفُولَةِ، وَنَحْتَفِلُ الآنَ مَعَ الجَالِيَةِ، وَسَأَزُورُ بَلَدَ أُسْرَتِي.
quiz.feedback: It moves through three tenses with accurate forms.

rows: say verb + preposition as one unit
add فِي بَعْضِ or لَيْسَ دَائِمًا

grammar.common_error: Overstating a cultural claim while speaking. Saying كُلُّ العَرَبِ is both inaccurate and avoidable; فِي بَعْضِ البُلْدَانِ costs one extra second.
grammar.challenge: Answer three cultural questions aloud in ninety seconds, each with a correct preposition, a reason and a qualifier.

builders.target: Build complete spoken answers from a past clause, a present clause and a qualified close.

builders.feedback: Each clause is accurate on its own, so any three different combinations make a complete answer.

mistakes.right: فِي بَعْضِ البُلْدَانِ يَحْتَفِلُ النَّاسُ بِهٰذِهِ الطَّرِيقَةِ.
mistakes.why: A universal claim about a whole population is inaccurate.
يَحْتَفِلُ requires بِـ.

listening.title: Listening: a candidate in the topic conversation
listening.script: المُمْتَحِنُ: صِفْ مُنَاسَبَةً ثَقَافِيَّةً مَرَرْتَ بِهَا. الطَّالِبَةُ: دَعْنِي أُفَكِّرُ. فِي العَامِ المَاضِي حَضَرْتُ حَفْلًا فِي المَرْكَزِ الثَّقَافِيِّ، وَتُزَيَّنُ القَاعَةُ عَادَةً بِالأَعْلَامِ وَالفَوَانِيسِ. عَفْوًا، أَقْصِدُ أَنَّهَا زُيِّنَتْ فِي ذٰلِكَ اليَوْمِ. المُمْتَحِنُ: وَهَلْ يَحْتَفِلُ كُلُّ النَّاسِ بِالطَّرِيقَةِ نَفْسِهَا؟ الطَّالِبَةُ: عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي لَا؛ فَفِي بَعْضِ البُلْدَانِ تَخْتَلِفُ العَادَاتُ، وَلَيْسَ دَائِمًا يَتَشَابَهُ الاحْتِفَالُ. المُمْتَحِنُ: وَمَا أَهَمِّيَّةُ اللُّغَةِ العَرَبِيَّةِ فِي حَيَاتِكِ؟ الطَّالِبَةُ: لَا يُمْكِنُ إِنْكَارُ أَنَّ اللُّغَةَ جُزْءٌ مِنَ الهُوِيَّةِ، وَأَعْتَزُّ بِهَا، وَسَأُوَاصِلُ تَعَلُّمَهَا.

questions.prompt: How does the student open?
questions.feedback: دَعْنِي أُفَكِّرُ buys a moment in Arabic.

questions.prompt: What does عَفْوًا، أَقْصِدُ signal?
questions.feedback: She corrects the general present to a specific past passive.

questions.prompt: How does she answer the question about everyone celebrating alike?
options: No, as far as she knows; customs differ
questions.feedback: عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي لَا؛ فَفِي بَعْضِ البُلْدَانِ تَخْتَلِفُ العَادَاتُ.

questions.prompt: Which opinion structure does she use?
questions.feedback: لَا يُمْكِنُ إِنْكَارُ أَنَّ introduces a strong supported claim.

questions.prompt: How does she close?
options: With a future commitment to keep learning

reading.title: Reading: a candidate's self-review
reading.text: قَبْلَ التَّقْيِيمِ النِّهَائِيِّ رَاجَعْتُ نِقَاطَ ضَعْفِي بِصَرَاحَةٍ. فِي البِدَايَةِ كُنْتُ أُخْطِئُ فِي حُرُوفِ الجَرِّ مَعَ الأَفْعَالِ الثَّقَافِيَّةِ، فَأَقُولُ نَحْتَفِلُ العِيدَ بَدَلَ نَحْتَفِلُ بِالعِيدِ. ثُمَّ تَدَرَّبْتُ عَلَى كُلِّ فِعْلٍ مَعَ حَرْفِ جَرِّهِ حَتَّى صَارَا وَحْدَةً وَاحِدَةً. وَكُنْتُ أُعَمِّمُ أَحْيَانًا فَأَقُولُ كُلُّ العَرَبِ، وَالآنَ أَقُولُ فِي بَعْضِ البُلْدَانِ أَوْ عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي. عَلَى الرَّغْمِ مِنْ ذٰلِكَ مَا زِلْتُ أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى تَحْسِينِ سُرْعَتِي فِي الرَّدِّ. وَفِي المُسْتَقْبَلِ سَأُرَكِّزُ عَلَى إِضَافَةِ سَبَبٍ فِي كُلِّ إِجَابَةٍ، وَأَطْمَحُ إِلَى أَنْ أَتَحَدَّثَ دُونَ تَرَدُّدٍ.

questions.prompt: What was the original weakness?
questions.feedback: كُنْتُ أُخْطِئُ فِي حُرُوفِ الجَرِّ مَعَ الأَفْعَالِ الثَّقَافِيَّةِ.

questions.feedback: مَا زِلْتُ أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى تَحْسِينِ سُرْعَتِي فِي الرَّدِّ.

differentiation.core: Answer four cultural questions aloud using the sentence frames, each with the right preposition.

final.prompt: The question is صِفْ مُنَاسَبَةً مَرَرْتَ بِهَا. Which answer fits?
final.feedback: Mirror the tense of the question.
يَحْتَفِلُ is fixed with بِـ.
عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي limits the claim to what you know.

options: حَضَرْتُ حَفْلًا فِي الطُّفُولَةِ، وَنَحْتَفِلُ الآنَ مَعَ الجَالِيَةِ، وَسَأَزُورُ بَلَدَ أُسْرَتِي.

rounds.feedback: أَنَّ takes an accusative noun.
The passive agrees with the feminine subject.

rounds.prompt: Repair: which phrase corrects a slip?
rounds.feedback: عَفْوًا، أَقْصِدُ introduces a self-correction.

rounds.prompt: Extension: which adds most to a bare answer?
rounds.feedback: A reason turns an answer into a response.
كَانَ plus a present verb is a past habit.

rounds.prompt: Vocabulary: which means “as far as I know”?
rounds.feedback: عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي limits a claim to your own knowledge.

rounds.prompt: Statistic: complete — ___ العَرَبِيَّةُ مِنْ أَوْسَعِ اللُّغَاتِ انْتِشَارًا.
rounds.feedback: يُعَدُّ مِنْ is the passive used for classification.
سَـ marks a future commitment.

rounds.prompt: Transfer: which full answer would score highest?
options: حَضَرْتُ حَفْلًا فِي العَامِ المَاضِي، وَنَحْتَفِلُ الآنَ بِالعِيدِ مَعَ الجَالِيَةِ، وَفِي بَعْضِ البُلْدَانِ تَخْتَلِفُ العَادَاتُ، وَسَأَزُورُ بَلَدَ أُسْرَتِي.
حَضَرْتُ حَفْلًا وَكُلُّ العَرَبِ مِثْلُنَا وَنَحْتَفِلُ العِيدَ.
أَحْضُرُ حَفْلًا فِي العَامِ المَاضِي وَسَأَحْضُرُ أَمْسِ.
rounds.feedback: Three tenses, the right preposition, a qualifier and a future plan.
